It is also submitted that the prosecutrix was a consenting party as she has resided with Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81934890/

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the charge sheet has already been filed, applicant is lodged in jail since 20/10/2022 and the final conclusion of trial is likely to take sufficient long time.

sentences.text: Hence, it is submitted that the bail application be allowed and he be released on bail.

sentences.text: Counsel for the respondent / State as well as the objector, on the other hand have opposed the prayer and it is submitted that no case for grant of bail is made out as the prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident as according to the scholar register, her date of birth is 19/10/2004.
sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Having considered the rival submissions, perusal of the case diary and also taking note of the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. wherein also, her age is stated to be 17 years and 11 months at the time of incident and the fact that she has resided with the applicant for around 14 days and further taking note of the fact that the applicant is lodged in jail since 20/10/2022 and final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time, in the considered opinion of this Court, the applicant's application deserves to be allowed.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is allowed.

sentences.text:
Per Justice Gajendra Singh:
IA No.728/2025 is preferred under section 430(1) of the BNSS, 2023 for suspension of execution of the sentence of sole appellant Devendra.
sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Appellant Devendra has been convicted under sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of the IPC and section 6 r/w section 5(l)
of the POCSO Act, 2012 and has been sentenced for 3 years, 5 years and 20 years RI and fine with default stipulation vide judgment dated 24.12.2024 in S.T.No.30/2022 by 2nd Addl. Sessions Judge and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Mahidpur, district Ujjain.
Appellant Devendra has been convicted and sentenced for kidnapping and committing penetrative sexual assault towards child victim (PW/1), aged 16 years 4 months during the period 03.06.2022 to 28.07.2022 and regarding which a crime no.150/2022 was registered at PS Raghavi, district Ujjain.
sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: This application is preferred on the ground that applicant is a young boy and he recently got married on 24.11.2024 and wife of the 2 CRA-397-2025 applicant has a right of cohabitation with the applicant/accused.
sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: Prosecutrix (PW/1) has not supported the case of prosecution in any manner and has been declared hostile.
sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: She herself has categorically stated that she had on her own went along with the applicant and had stayed with him in different places and also admitted in para-13 of cross examination that she was major at the time of incident.
sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: The trial court passed the judgment by convicting the applicant merely on the statement of the interested witnesses who after a plan and strategy implicated the present appellant falsely.
sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: The trial court was wrong in not considering the material omissions and contradictions in the statement of prosecution witnesses.
sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: There are serious omissions and contradictions in the statement of the witnesses.
sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: The entire prosecution story is doubtful.
sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: There is no iota of material against the appellant for which he has been convicted.
sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: The investigating agency has dealt with the case through casual investigation.
sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025.json

State has opposed the application by filing reply through document no.1129/2025 and submitted that age of the prosecutrix has been proved by cogent evidence and the act of the penetrative sexual Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68282565/
1 assault has been proved through DNA fingerprint report Ex.P/29.

sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: Counsel for the complainant i.e. father of the victim (PW/1) also filed objection through IA No.3876/2025 and opposed the suspension of the sentence.
sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: It was argued that the offence under section 366 of IPC is against the lawful guardian of child.
sentences._hearing_file: Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025.json

sentences.text:

IA No.728/2025 is preferred under section 430(1) of the BNSS, 2023 for suspension of execution of the sentence of sole appellant Devendra.
opennyai_summary.7_April_2025__facts:
Appellant Devendra has been convicted under sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of the IPC and section 6 r/w section 5(l)
of the POCSO Act, 2012 and has been sentenced for 3 years, 5 years and 20 years RI and fine with default stipulation vide judgment dated 24.12.2024 in S.T.No.30/2022 by 2nd Addl. Sessions Judge and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Mahidpur, district Ujjain.
Appellant Devendra has been convicted and sentenced for kidnapping and committing penetrative sexual assault towards child victim (PW/1), aged 16 years 4 months during the period 03.06.2022 to 28.07.2022 and regarding which a crime no.150/2022 was registered at PS Raghavi, district Ujjain.
She herself has categorically stated that she had on her own went along with the applicant and had stayed with him in different places and also admitted in para-13 of cross examination that she was major at the time of incident.
The trial court passed the judgment by convicting the applicant merely on the statement of the interested witnesses who after a plan and strategy implicated the present appellant falsely.
The trial court was wrong in not considering the material omissions and contradictions in the statement of prosecution witnesses.
opennyai_summary.7_April_2025__ANALYSIS:
There are serious omissions and contradictions in the statement of the witnesses.
There is no iota of material against the appellant for which he has been convicted.
State has opposed the application by filing reply through document no.1129/2025 and submitted that age of the prosecutrix has been proved by cogent evidence and the act of the penetrative sexual Devendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68282565/
1 assault has been proved through DNA fingerprint report Ex.P/29.
It was argued that the offence under section 366 of IPC is against the lawful guardian of child.
The facts of the other referred cases also are not similar as either date of birth is not proved through certificate of Board examination or period of custody was significant or the act was not proved through scientific evidence of DNA fingerprint report.
opennyai_summary.7_April_2025__decision:
Accordingly, we are not inclined to suspend the sentence of the appellant at present.
I.A.No.728/2025 is accordingly rejected.

opennyai_summary.final__decision:
Appellant has been convicted under Sections 376(3), 376(2)(I)(F) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 6 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years with fine of Rs. 1000/-, R.I.
for 10 years with fine of Rs. 500/- and R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs. 500/- with default stipulations.
Medical examination report is also against prosecution.
Appellant is in jail since last 7 years.
In these circumstances, appellant's sentence may be suspended and he may be released on bail.
